description: ASTRAVANT is a six-member team passionate about space, technology, AI, and geospatial problem-solving. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are working on identifying Earth locations that resemble environments on the Moon and Mars. Our goal is to use NASA data and intelligent analysis to evaluate potential analog sites for rover testing, astronaut training, habitat research, and future planetary exploration.

𝐏𝐑𝐎𝐁𝐋𝐄𝐌
Moon and Mars missions need Earth sites to test rovers, drills and equipment, but the right site depends on the mission and analog data is scattered.

𝐒𝐎𝐋𝐔𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍
ASTRANOVUS is a web platform that finds Earth regions matching a specific Moon or Mars mission goal. You pick a destination (Moon or Mars), one of 12 tests (like ice drilling, rover driving, habitats or geology) and a target site, such as Shackleton crater or Jezero crater. It then ranks the best Earth regions on an interactive map.

𝐍𝐀𝐒𝐀 𝐃𝐀𝐓𝐀
It compares 3,435 regions using NASA POWER, MODIS, GPM, ASTER and SRTM data.

𝐇𝐎𝐍𝐄𝐒𝐓 𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐔𝐋𝐓𝐒
Each result shows its score, data support, matches, gaps and what Earth can't copy. Checked against Atacama, Devon Island and Antarctica.

𝐖𝐇𝐘 𝐈𝐓 𝐌𝐀𝐓𝐓𝐄𝐑𝐒
Faster, clearer test-site planning for Artemis and future Mars missions.
details:
Live Platform: https://astranovus.vercel.app
GitHub Repository: https://github.com/asharr-1shera23z/Astranovus-NASA-Space-Apps-Challenge-2026
Project Presentation (PPT): https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1xIvVdQpN46I51s0pMwuT2aAtRG4R8WlJ/edit?usp=sharing

Demo Video (30 seconds): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jfA9J_e-m-OHKx1om9QyQR0fs9GU41uN/view?usp=sharing

1. THE PROBLEM

As NASA prepares for future Moon bases and human missions to Mars, researchers need suitable locations on Earth to test technologies, conduct experiments and prepare for planetary exploration.

However, different missions require different environments. Testing a rover requires challenging terrain, while testing ice-extraction equipment requires cold, ice-rich conditions. Although several Earth analog sites are already known, information about them is spread across scientific studies and datasets, making it difficult to identify the most suitable location for a specific mission.

2. WHAT WE BUILT

ASTRANOVUS is an interactive, data-driven Earth Analog Discovery platform developed by Team Astravant.

It helps researchers identify, rank and explore locations on Earth that share important environmental characteristics with specific regions on the Moon and Mars.

Instead of simply finding places that look like another planet, ASTRANOVUS focuses on matching Earth environments to actual mission requirements, helping users understand which locations are suitable for particular exploration activities and why.

3. HOW ASTRANOVUS WORKS

Our platform follows a straightforward process:

  1. Choose a Destination: Select the Moon or Mars.
  2. Define a Mission: Choose from 12 exploration scenarios, including water-ice extraction, rover mobility, dust and thermal testing, habitat operations, geology and astrobiology.
  3. Select a Planetary Reference: Choose from 9 reference sites, including Shackleton Crater, Jezero Crater and the Martian ice-rich plains of Arcadia Planitia.
  4. Analyze Earth Environments: Our Python-based engine evaluates 3,435 Earth land grid cells at 2.5° resolution using eight environmental dimensions: temperature, aridity, vegetation, terrain, surface and rock characteristics, snow and ice, polar-light indicators and day-night temperature variation.
  5. Explore the Results: The most suitable regions appear on an interactive world map and 3D globe, with similarity scores, confidence indicators, data coverage and supporting scientific evidence.

Users can explore recommended regions and understand the environmental factors influencing each result.

4. NASA DATA & SCIENTIFIC APPROACH

ASTRANOVUS combines NASA Earth observation data with planetary reference information to perform mission-specific environmental comparisons.

Earth observation datasets include:

  • NASA POWER: Temperature and climate information.
  • MODIS: Land surface temperature, vegetation and 10 years of snow-cover observations.
  • GPM IMERG: Precipitation and aridity analysis.
  • ASTER GED: Surface properties useful for environmental and geological interpretation.
  • SRTM and Antarctic elevation data: Terrain elevation and topographic analysis.

We also assembled 35 planetary reference measurements from NASA, JPL, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and USGS resources to help characterize the selected Moon and Mars environments.

Our explainable Python scoring engine processes these datasets, converts environmental observations into comparable indicators and applies mission-specific weights to rank Earth locations.

Unlike a black-box recommendation system, ASTRANOVUS is designed to show which environmental factors contribute to each score.

5. KEY FEATURES & BENEFITS

  • Mission-Specific Recommendations: Locations are ranked according to the selected exploration objective rather than a general Moon-like or Mars-like description.
  • Interactive Geospatial Exploration: Users can examine candidate regions using an interactive map and 3D globe.
  • Explainable Similarity Scores: Each recommendation highlights matching conditions, missing evidence and important limitations.
  • Scientific Transparency: Missing values are not invented, and estimated measurements or indirect indicators are clearly identified.
  • Accessible Research Tool: ASTRANOVUS is freely accessible through a web browser, helping researchers and students explore planetary science without specialized hardware.

6. TECHNOLOGIES & DEVELOPMENT TOOLS

We developed ASTRANOVUS using a combination of modern web technologies, Python-based scientific computing and geospatial data processing.

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet maps and interactive 3D globe visualization.
  • Backend & Data Processing: Python, FastAPI, pandas and NumPy.
  • Testing & Quality Assurance: pytest, Vitest and data validation checks.
  • Deployment & Collaboration: Vercel, Render and GitHub.
  • Hardware: Standard laptops, demonstrating that meaningful planetary data analysis can be developed using accessible computing resources.

7. WHAT MAKES ASTRANOVUS CREATIVE?

ASTRANOVUS introduces a different approach to Earth analog discovery by connecting planetary exploration objectives directly with measurable environmental conditions.

  • Mission-First Analysis: The same Earth region may be highly suitable for rover mobility testing but unsuitable for ice extraction. Our platform accounts for these differences instead of assigning one general planetary similarity score.
  • Explainable Recommendations: Rather than displaying only a ranking, ASTRANOVUS explains the environmental factors behind it and identifies uncertainty or missing evidence.
  • Beyond Famous Analog Sites: In addition to established Earth analogs, the platform supports exploring less-studied candidate regions, including potential locations in Pakistan. Known analogs and new hypotheses are distinguished to avoid presenting unverified candidates as established sites.
  • Interactive Scientific Exploration: By combining NASA datasets, mission-specific scoring and geographic visualization, ASTRANOVUS makes complex planetary comparisons easier to explore and understand.

8. SCIENTIFIC ACCURACY & LIMITATIONS

We prioritized scientific transparency throughout the development process.

  • Validation: We compared the scoring engine’s recommendations with established Earth analog sites, including the Atacama Desert, Devon Island and Antarctica’s McMurdo Dry Valleys. These comparisons help assess the system’s behavior and reveal where additional evidence is required.
  • Data Limitations: Some conditions, particularly underground environments such as lava tubes, cannot be reliably identified using the available satellite observations. These limitations are acknowledged rather than treated as confirmed matches.
  • Spatial Resolution: Our 2.5° global grid provides broad regional screening, not precise field-site identification. Promising regions therefore require further investigation using higher-resolution datasets and field observations.
  • Planetary Differences: Earth’s gravity, atmosphere and radiation environment differ substantially from those of the Moon and Mars. Our scores represent similarity in selected test conditions, not complete planetary equivalence or certified mission-site suitability.

9. INTENDED IMPACT & FUTURE SCOPE

ASTRANOVUS aims to make Earth analog discovery more efficient, transparent and accessible.

By bringing environmental datasets, mission requirements, geographic visualization and explainable recommendations together, it can help researchers narrow down promising locations for rover testing, resource-extraction experiments, habitat research and planetary geology studies.

The platform also creates educational opportunities for students and researchers worldwide, including in Pakistan, by making NASA-based planetary research easier to explore.

In the future, ASTRANOVUS could be expanded with higher-resolution environmental data, additional planetary reference sites, improved geological indicators and field-based validation.

Our long-term vision is to support Earth-based research and technology testing that contributes to Artemis and future Mars exploration missions.

ASTRANOVUS: Finding the Right Earth Environments for Moon and Mars Exploration.
